fichas.title: Rehearsal rooms
fichas.summary: Theatre rehearsal provision includes at least one rehearsal stage corresponding in dimensions to the main stage. Multipurpose theatres and opera houses may also require orchestra and chorus rehearsal rooms, soloist rehearsal rooms, and a ballet room. The page illustrates typical plans for large-stage, chorus, and orchestra rehearsals.
uses: Rehearsing productions away from the main stage

Rehearsal rooms
Every theatre needs at least one rehearsal stage to back up the main
stage. For example, a small theatre: the main stage has the scenery
of the current play and the rehearsals take place on the rehearsal
stage. The dimensions should correspond to the main stage. Typical
floor plan of the rehearsal stage of a traditional theatre -7 0. Multipurpose theatres and opera houses also require: orchestra rehearsal
room -7 e, chorus rehearsal room -7 e, soloist rehearsal room and
ballet room.
Experimental theatres
These also require, in reduced form, staff and rehearsal rooms,
workshops and stores, if in continual operation.

ca. 2.Q-2.4m2Jmusician

ca. 8.0-10m3fmusician

~

Technical rooms
Rooms for transformer, medium- and low-voltage switchgear,
emergency power supply batteries, air conditioning and ventilation
plant, water supply (rainwater system), according to local conditions
and specialist design work.
Public rooms
The classical Italian opera had only narrow entrances and stairs,
with no actual foyer. This makes the generous public rooms at the
Grand Opera in Paris particularly impressive. The Vienna theatre
fire in 1881 led to extensive changes: the audience is now required
to have enclosed emergency stairs for each tier. This requirement
continues in principle today (Public Assembly Regulations).

F-------------------------CI

C) Orchestra rehearsal room, typical plan

In the traditional theatre, the foyers are split into: actual foyer
(lobby), restaurant (buffet), smoker's foyer. Area of the foyers
0.8-2.0 m2/spectator (more realistic is 0.6-0.8 m2/spectator). The
function of the foyer has changed today: it must include provision
for exhibitions, performances and regular plays there.

3 tickets

Cloakrooms
Per 100 visitors: 4 running m of rail. Sometimes lockers are also
provided: one locker for every four visitors. The foyer is also a
waiting and queuing room, and has the usual extent of associated
WCs: one WC/1 00 people. 1fa gents, 2fa ladies; min. one gents' and
one ladies' WC. Total number of sanitary facilities: -7 p. 216 G).
Entrance hall (lobby) with day and evening cash desks, which
should be opposite each other.

fichas.title: Technical rooms
fichas.summary: Technical rooms accommodate building services and electrical infrastructure. Their provision is determined by local conditions and specialist design work.
uses: Providing emergency power, ventilation, air conditioning, and water-supply services
figure_refs: 4 Entrance floor of Heilbronn City Theatre

fichas.title: Public rooms and foyers
fichas.summary: Traditional theatre foyers may be divided into a lobby, restaurant or buffet, and smokers’ foyer. Contemporary foyers are also expected to support exhibitions, performances, and regular plays. The text gives approximate foyer area per spectator and notes that a more realistic range may be lower.

dimensions.label: Foyer area per spectator
dimensions.context: General stated area range for theatre foyers.

dimensions.label: Foyer area per spectator, more realistic
dimensions.context: More realistic foyer area range stated in the text.

figure_refs: 4 Entrance floor of Heilbronn City Theatre

fichas.title: Cloakrooms, queues, and sanitary facilities
fichas.summary: Cloakroom provision is expressed per visitor, with optional lockers. The foyer also serves as a waiting and queuing area, with associated WCs. The text specifies WC proportions for men and women and minimum provision of one WC for each.

Rehearsal rooms
Every theatre needs at least one rehearsal stage to back up the main
stage. For example, a small theatre: the main stage has the scenery
of the current play and the rehearsals take place on the rehearsal
stage. The dimensions should correspond to the main stage. Typical
floor plan of the rehearsal stage of a traditional theatre -7 0. Multipurpose theatres and opera houses also require: orchestra rehearsal
room -7 e, chorus rehearsal room -7 e, soloist rehearsal room and
ballet room.
Experimental theatres
These also require, in reduced form, staff and rehearsal rooms,
workshops and stores, if in continual operation.

Rooms for transformer, medium- and low-voltage switchgear,
emergency power supply batteries, air conditioning and ventilation
plant, water supply (rainwater system), according to local conditions
and specialist design work.
Public rooms
The classical Italian opera had only narrow entrances and stairs,
with no actual foyer. This makes the generous public rooms at the
Grand Opera in Paris particularly impressive. The Vienna theatre
fire in 1881 led to extensive changes: the audience is now required
to have enclosed emergency stairs for each tier. This requirement
continues in principle today (Public Assembly Regulations).

F-------------------------CI

C) Orchestra rehearsal room, typical plan

0.8-2.0 m2/spectator (more realistic is 0.6-0.8 m2/spectator). The
function of the foyer has changed today: it must include provision
for exhibitions, performances and regular plays there.

3 tickets

Cloakrooms
Per 100 visitors: 4 running m of rail. Sometimes lockers are also
provided: one locker for every four visitors. The foyer is also a
waiting and queuing room, and has the usual extent of associated
WCs: one WC/1 00 people. 1fa gents, 2fa ladies; min. one gents' and
one ladies' WC. Total number of sanitary facilities: -7 p. 216 G).
Entrance hall (lobby) with day and evening cash desks, which
